page: Microsoft Azure E32s_v4 is a memory-optimized virtual machine provisioned on Microsoft Hyper-V. The system is driven by an Intel Xeon Platinum 8272CL processor running at a base clock of 2.6 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. Hardware resources comprise 16 physical cores configured with two threads per core to deliver 32 dedicated vCPUs, alongside a 35 MB L3 cache, 1.0 MB L2 cache, and 32 KB L1 data cache per core. Memory capacity is substantial, providing 256.0 GB of RAM configured at an 8.0 GB per vCPU ratio. This instance does not include integrated local disk storage or hardware accelerators such as GPUs.

Benchmark outcomes demonstrate solid mid-range capabilities across compute and memory workloads. The multi-core profile shows average performance tiers with a Geekbench multi-core score of 10,843.0 and a PassMark CPU score of 27,507.6. However, single-core execution presents a bottleneck, as indicated by a stress-ng single-core score of 1,412.79, which ranks in the bottom 25 percent. Instruction set capabilities include AVX, AVX-512F, and AVX-512 VNNI, helping PassMark extended instructions reach 28,366.1. Memory throughput remains balanced, offering 90.27 GB/sec for uncached large-block reads and 43.64 GB/sec for writes.

Given its dedicated resource allocation, the high memory-to-vCPU ratio yields qualitative resource efficiency for setups bounded strictly by RAM capacity rather than raw compute speed. In-memory caching operations, such as Redis SET operations at 26.54 million operations per second, along with database-related benchmarks, perform reliably within middle-tier expectations. Without local ephemeral NVMe disks, storage-bound workloads must utilize attached remote network volumes, making the E32s_v4 most suited for enterprise in-memory databases, distributed caches, big data processing, and large-scale enterprise application servers.
description: Microsoft Azure E32s_v4 is a memory-optimized virtual machine powered by an Intel Xeon 8272CL processor running at 2.6 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. It provides 32 dedicated vCPUs across 16 physical cores and 256.0 GB of system RAM, yielding a high ratio of 8.0 GB of memory per core. The instance includes no bundled local storage and features zero GPUs. Performance benchmarks show balanced mid-tier results across multi-core compute, memory operations, and compression tasks, achieving a Geekbench multi-core score of 10,843.0 and Redis throughput of 26.54 million SET operations per second. However, single-core compute ranks in the lower percentiles. The E32s_v4 represents a cost-effective choice for memory-dense architectures, making it suitable for in-memory databases, large Redis caches, data transformation pipelines, and enterprise application deployments.
